Deadlift Guide

Learn how to deadlift with a stronger setup, avoid common mistakes, progress safely, and track deadlift workouts in LogWise.

QUICK FACTS
Primary muscles
Back, glutes, hamstrings, quads, grip
Equipment
Barbell and plates
Movement pattern
Hip hinge and pull
Best for
Total-body strength and posterior-chain loading
FORM GUIDE

How to do the Deadlift

  1. Stand with the bar over the midfoot and place your feet around hip width.
  2. Hinge down, grip the bar, and bring the shins to the bar without pushing it forward.
  3. Brace hard, pull the slack out of the bar, and keep the chest proud.
  4. Push the floor away while the bar stays close to the legs.
  5. Lock out by driving the hips through, then lower the bar with control.
COMMON MISTAKES

Keep the lift honest

  • Starting with the bar too far from the body.
  • Rounding the back because the brace or setup was rushed.
  • Yanking the bar off the floor before tension is built.
  • Turning every deadlift session into a maximal test.
HOW TO PROGRESS

Make progress measurable

  • Progress deadlift volume conservatively because heavy pulls are expensive to recover from.
  • Use top sets plus back-off sets if straight heavy volume beats you up.
  • Track RIR and bar speed notes so you can tell a strong pull from a forced pull.
  • Rotate variations only when they solve a clear problem, not just because the lift feels hard.

Use the workout volume calculator when sets, reps, or load change enough that recovery becomes harder to judge.

TRACKING TIPS

What to log in LogWise

  • Log stance, grip, straps, belt use, and whether reps were touch-and-go or reset.
  • Track weekly pulling volume alongside rows, pull-ups, and Romanian deadlifts.
  • Use notes to separate technical misses from strength misses.

If you want a paper structure first, the workout log template captures the same basics: sets, reps, weight, RIR, and notes.

LogWise cues

  • Bar over mid-foot; shins should contact the bar before pulling.
  • Drive hips through at the top — maintain neutral spine, no rounding.
  • Take a deep breath and brace core before each rep (Valsalva maneuver).
  • Keep bar close to body throughout — don't let it drift forward.

Track the useful numbers

For this lift, the most useful history is simple: top set, back-off sets, total working volume, RIR, and short technique notes.
